findings.original: The value of labour-power, as dependent on its wear and tear, increases with the duration of its functioning
findings.rewrite: Because the value of labor-power depends on its wear and tear, it increases with the length of time that labor-power is at work
findings.problem: "as dependent on" can mean "since it depends on" or "insofar as it depends on". The rewrite chooses the causal reading and turns it into a flat claim that the value of labor-power (as a whole) depends on wear and tear.
findings.fix: "The value of labor-power, as it depends on its wear and tear, increases with the length of time that labor-power is at work, and it increases faster than that time does."

notes_review: The logged calls are sound. In p005 the change of "3s." to "3d." is the only possible reading: a day's value of 3s. = 36d., so 36d. ÷ 10 hours = 3 3/5d., 36d. ÷ 12 = 3d. and 36d. ÷ 15 = 2 2/5d., and an hourly price of "3s." would equal a whole day's value and could not be a "fall" from 3 3/5d., so the fix stands. Keeping "felling", the reversed "2s. or 1s. 6d." and the stray mark in the p009 formula as printed is correct.
summary: Fidelity is high. All the hourly-price arithmetic, the overtime evidence and the bakers' testimony are kept with their figures and attributions, and the irony ("amenities", "young immortals", the Bibles) is intact. The prose reads plainly.
